summary: II Preterit supplies the missing event box; Detransitive Part. Pass. describes continuing confinement across first-, second- and third-person patients, and plural animals.
Unaugmented ḥbiso/ḥbisoyo/ḥbisoye contrast with mḥabso/mḥabasto/mḥabse. Lookup confirms a separate ḥbš I, so semantics alone cannot assign the unaugmented series to a new ḥbs I.
Copular predication of a prisoner noun or adjective does not establish a productive verbal formation; retained as research evidence rather than new published morphology.

Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation, not an edition translation; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are inherited in the reading layout and are not repeated in this JSON.

Round 1 withheld I on isolated prisoner adjectives alone. Jan now supplies ḥbəsənne, ḥəbsənne, ḥbəslox and ḥbəsile with explicit confinement events; this is new finite evidence for I, not a second proposal of II.
ḥbiso/ḥbise with copula or fyš describe enduring confinement, while ḥbisi with coordinated returned refugees is an event in the Detransitive Preterit.
Form lookup and separate ḥbš entry were checked. s/š and II/I relations remain etymological/editorial questions, not automatic corrections. No unattested Infectum is supplied.
Resolve ḥbiso at 57/75, ḥbisoyo at 57/86 and ḥbisoye at 89/114: Arabic-derived prisoner adjective/noun, ḥbs I Detransitive Part. Pass., or an s-variant related to ḥbš I?
Does mḥabasto in 107/108 describe imposed confinement or voluntary staying in the room? The same resulting-state gloss is retained without claiming a separate Detransitive function.
Does Jan s beside inherited ḥbš reflect dialect, Arabic contact or a distinct lexical history? The published proposal preserves the attested spelling.
Confirm segmentation of ḥbəsile at Jan 2.22/4001 and 4003. The basic Preterit ḥbəsle is inferred from attested inflections; obtain an Infectum from a speaker.
Camels as confined patients extend the existing imprisonment meaning; no separate animal sense.
